recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** instructed officials to pursue legal action regarding the Mekedatu dam issue after a meeting with experts and legal luminaries on Monday. The meeting, attended by **Ministers N. Anand**, **Aadhav Arjuna**, and **R. Nirmalkumar**, and senior officials, considered the Supreme Court's November 2025 ruling that only the Central Water Commission could determine if the project complied with previous judgments.  The review petition against this verdict was dismissed in December 2025, prompting **Vijay** to direct expedited legal action.

recent_articles.title: Government polytechnics in Tamil Nadu record near total placement this year - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Government polytechnic colleges** in Tamil Nadu have achieved over 93% placement for their diploma students in the academic year 2025-26, a notable development amidst rising interest in engineering.  The **Directorate of Technical Education (DoTE)** attributes this success to the vocational and trade-specific skills imparted by diploma courses, which often come with higher starting salaries than traditional engineering degrees. While some students opted for lateral entry into engineering programs, the placement rate remains high, with employers offering competitive packages. However, government-aided and self-financing polytechnics face challenges in attracting student patronage, leading to a phase-wise shutdown of some institutions.

recent_articles.title: T.N. Government appoints T.S Anbu as ADGP (Law and Order); Arun to head DVAC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Tamil Nadu government** appointed **T.S. Anbu**, a 2001-batch IPS officer, as the new ADGP, Law and Order, replacing **Maheshwar Dayal**.  **Anbu**, who has served in various capacities including Deputy Commissioner of Police and Superintendent of Police, Madurai, will oversee law and order amidst recent incidents of crime. The government also appointed **A. Arun**, former Chennai Police Commissioner, as Director, Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC).

recent_articles.title: Man held on charge of theft - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajan alias Natarajan**, a 61-year-old Tamil Nadu native, has been arrested in connection with the theft of 45 sovereigns of gold ornaments from a house in Bekal.  The **Bekal police** recovered the stolen jewelry from a hideout on Netaji Road near Kannur railway station following a complaint filed by the homeowner.

recent_articles.title: Disambiguating a year of flux: expert panels at The Hindu Huddle, 2026 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The sixth edition of The Hindu Group's ideas conclave, The Hindu Huddle, will be held in Bengaluru on June 5 and 6, 2026.  **Siddaramaiah**, **D.K. Shivakumar**, and other Chief Ministers from across the country will participate alongside Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship **Jayant Chaudhary**, **Omar Abdullah**, **A. Revanth Reddy**, and **K.G. Arunraj**. The event will feature discussions on topics such as tariffs' impact on the Indian economy, diplomacy in managing crises, and artificial intelligence's influence on various aspects of life.  **The Hindu Huddle** is presented by the Sami-Sabinsa Group and co-powered by the Government of Telangana.

recent_articles.title: National president Nabin asks BJP State unit not to be complacent while citing T.N. example of Opposition not benefitting from DMK’s failure - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nitin Nabin**, **BJP** national president, warned the Karnataka unit to avoid complacency after the Tamil Nadu elections where the opposition AIADMK did not benefit despite anti-incumbency. He urged them to project themselves as a strong alternative and focus on public awareness against the Congress government's failures.  He also emphasized the need for a pro-people struggle and a comprehensive action plan for upcoming elections, including bypolls and Legislative Council elections. **Nabin** accused the Congress of using its government as an ATM to fund its national activities.

recent_articles.title: MMK will continue its alliance with DMK, says Jawahirullah - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Manithaneya Makkal Katchi (MMK)** president M.H. Jawahirullah clarified that the party's recent resolution to contest on its own symbol was not due to disappointment over a lack of ministerial positions in the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government. The MMK contested under the DMK’s ‘Rising Sun’ symbol in previous elections, and this decision was made based on ground realities and political circumstances.  The party's registration was cancelled after failing to contest on its own symbol, prompting the resolution for future elections.

recent_articles.title: Vijay should strongly oppose Mekedatu dam plan: Seeman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Seeman**, chief co-ordinator of **Naam Tamilar Katchi**, criticized **D.K. Shivakumar**, Karnataka's deputy Chief Minister, for his statement that Tamil Nadu does not have the right to oppose the Karnataka government's plan to build a dam at Mekedatu across the Cauvery river.  **Seeman** called the statement arrogant and said it indicated an attempt by **Karnataka** to claim exclusive ownership over the Cauvery river water rights. He urged **Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay** to register strong opposition to the project.

recent_articles.title: BJP tried to stitch coalition govt. in Tamil Nadu with DMK and AIADMK on election result day: Congress MP Manickam Tagore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** MP B. Manickam Tagore accused **DMK** leader Udhayanidhi Stalin of attempting to form a coalition government with the **AIADMK** to prevent TVK president C. Joseph Vijay from becoming Chief Minister.  He claimed that the **DMK**'s actions were orchestrated by the **BJP**, and that they will soon strike an understanding with the party, potentially leading to DMK MPs abstaining from voting against the BJP-led government in Parliament.  **Girish Chodankar**, Congress's in-charge for Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, responded to the accusations by stating that the attacks on the Congress should not be directed at the people of Tamil Nadu who voted.

recent_articles.title: SC’s revival of Section 124A for consenting accused brings back a colonial law the country did not want - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Supreme Court** has revived Section 124A (sedition) proceedings, despite its previous agreement that the provision was outdated and oppressive. The court's May 21 clarification allows for trials under the section to proceed on merits, but this decision does not address the constitutionality of the law itself, which is still being challenged in separate petitions.  The court’s action has created practical challenges, particularly regarding situations where accused individuals may consent to proceedings while co-accused refuse.

recent_articles.title: Congress factions in Kerala ‘wishcasting’ for their respective loyalists as KPCC president’s post comes up for grabs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** factions in Kerala are engaged in a power struggle for the upcoming KPCC president position, with **Sunny Joseph**, current KPCC president, joining the government. The **All India Congress Committee (AICC)** is reportedly set to intervene and re-organize the party's leadership structure, including the KPCC presidency, amidst concerns about internal divisions hindering past UDF governments.  The AICC has emphasized social demographics, caste balance, and merit as key considerations for selecting the next KPCC president.

recent_articles.title: Steps will be taken to modernise prison administration: T.N. Law Minister Nirmalkumar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **R. Nirmalkumar**, Tamil Nadu Minister for Law, emphasized the need for prison modernization in the state, including using digital technologies to enhance visitor screening and prevent contraband smuggling.  He inspected the Central Prison at Puzhal and noted the need for improved hospital equipment and basic amenities for the 1,500 inmates housed there. **Nirmalkumar** also pledged to explore legal aid options for remand prisoners held beyond their stipulated periods and directed both the Electricity and Prisons departments to avoid unnecessary administrative transfers.
